recipes.name: Slow Cooker Moscow Chicken
ingredients_raw: 1 (10 fluid ounce) bottle Russian-style salad dressing

steps.text: Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook chicken until well browned on both sides. Allow chicken to cool slightly.

Wrap each thigh in a piece of bacon, and place in slow cooker. Sprinkle garlic and ginger over the chicken; top with Russian dressing. Cook on Low heat for 5 to 6 hours. Season to taste with salt and pepper.

raw_recipe.headline: Slow Cooker Moscow Chicken
raw_recipe.description: Chicken thighs turn tender and delicious when wrapped in smokey bacon and slow cooked with Russian dressing.

review.reviewBody: very tender and YUMMY...I made some changes to make it EVEN EASIER! 1) I browned the thighs, then wrapped with bacon and placed in crock pot. 2) Then I (because I'm not a fan of that dressing) put BBQ sauce over the thighs 3) I cooked on high for 3 hours (was short on time) TASTED GREAT!!! Thanks for the recipe! :)

Everyone loved this!!! I read the reviews and took a few tips from them. I sliced 3 yellow onions and placed at the bottom of the crockpot. I also pre-cooked the bacon and browned the chicken in the bacon grease. Thanks for the recipe!!
Very easy recipe. Taste great. I made this for a crowd and nothing was left over. I precooked the bacon and place the chicken on a bed of onions. Very good! Everyone was pleased.

Very easy & good tasting. I heeded other reviewers' warnings about the grease level & partially cooked the bacon in the microwave before wrapping it over the chicken. I made the "Russian Salad Dressing" recipe from this site and used chopped white onion since I had no green onions. I used bone-in, skin on thighs which I quickly browned in hot oil, then drained on paper towels before placing in the crock pot. I cooked it for 5 hours. It was tender juicy and did not fall apart. The dressing did not separate as one reviewer experienced. They may have used a different recipe for the Russian dressing that included sour cream, causing it to separate. Also, the folks whose chicken was done early may have over-browned it before putting it in the crock-pot. Overall, this is a great recipe. I will be making it again.

This was excellent and so easy - I did not brown the chicken I used frozen boneless skinless thighs, wrapped with bacon - and I couldn't find Russian dressing so I used Ken's Sun dried Tomato Vinaigrette (much like Russian dressing) and it was delicious. My husband does not like fresh ginger but said it was some of the best chicken he'd ever had and asked for to become a regular. I mixed the sauce in a bowl and poured it over the bacon wrapped thighs.

I really enjoyed the flavor. However the bacon in the crockpot remained soggy, and half the sauce was bacon grease. So I put the oven on 400 and baked for 20 min to make the bacon edible. The sauce although tastes, was too greasy, and not enough to pour over rice. Next time I will halfway cook the bacon getting rid of half the grease, and I wouldn't wrap it...double Russian dressing, and skip the crock pot all together. I would layer chicken on bottom garlic, ginger, green onions, dressing and bacon laid on top. Cover and bake at 400 for 30 min and uncovered for 20 with bacon on top to crisp.

My family of picky eaters loves this dish. The only suggestion is please cook your bacon a bit first so it crisps up nicely when the dish is done instead of being limp and fatty. The other thing I do different is use 8 thighs instead because there are more of us, and since we love the sauce it makes, I use a whole 16 ounce bottle of Wish Bone Russian dressing and of course increase the garlic and ginger to go along with that. The sauce is WONDERFUL over rice, so you are going to want extra.

This was easy to prepare and was very very good. My boyfriend absolutely loved it. We couldn't find Russian dressing at the local grocery store (seriously, it was ridiculous!) so I had to make it from scratch. Sadly, the dressing separated during cooking and didn't look too appetizing in the crock but it still tasted amazing. Next time (and there will certainly be a next time, we loved this) I'll definitely make sure to use bottled dressing as that should help remedy the separation problem and make this even better. Also, I did microwave the bacon for a short time before wrapping the chicken. I'm not sure it was necessary but it turned out very nicely.

Everyone loved to moist chicken and the sauce, Getting the bacon to crisp was a problem but the broiler worked with the chicken on a jelly roll pan lined with non stick foil. I addeed more than 2 green onions and about one more clove of garlic. The sauce will be great on other meats as well. Love it and will make it again and again.

Really great dish, it smelled delicious! I used chicken breasts instead of thighs and they turned out great. I cooked the bacon a bit (not fully) beforehand which was a good choice. I served this over basmati rice.

Our family loves this recipe an make it at least once a month. I slightly brown the bacon first, then cook the chicken in the bacon grease. Russian dressing is hard to find but I substituted Country French as I noted someone else had done.
Flavor was good, easy to prepare, but the bacon made this dish greasy.

This was a bit odd. I used Catalina dressing but added horseradish to bring it closer to Russian and cayenne to tame the sweetness. I mostly cooked the bacon per suggestions and added a bed of sliced onion to the bottom of the crock. I wanted it to be super simple for his dinner so added some rice, chicken broth and tossed a few slices of zucchini for a one pot meal. Like others have mentioned, it has a greasy consistency that isn't the best. It had a unique smell and the taste wasn't bad, but prob won't try again.

It wasn't bad but it wasn't great either. My son said it was okay but not one to make again. I used pre-cooked bacon which worked well. It just didn't have a ton of flavor overall and was still greasy.

It's not very often that everyone in the family loves a dish. This scored with everyone! It is delicious, simple and satisfying. This one is a keeper for sure. I didn't have Russian dressing so I substituted with French dressing. Perfect for a winter evening!
It was just okay. We ate it but would not make it again. Just didn't wow any of us.

I doubles the recipe and made this for a birthday dinner. It went over like a rocket! Everyone loved it. The chicken was so tender and the flavor of bacon put it over the top. I saved a few pieces to have for dinner the next day, it was that good!

I made the homemade Russian dressing which was delicious but it didn't hold the flavors when cooked with the chicken. Bacon was soggy so I follow another's suggestion and baked it for 20 mins which helped. Sauce too greasy. Not a winner for me unfortunately.
I was concerned as the smell when taking it out of the cooker was pretty bad, but its actually very delicious. Would make it again for sure.
Too sour, added soy sauce and still too sour!
